fields.label: Certificate Authority ID
fields.help: The user provided Resource ID for this Certificate Authority.

fields.label: Deletion Policy
fields.help: Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance.

fields.label: Deletion Protection
fields.help: Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the CertificateAuthority.

fields.label: Desired State
fields.help: Desired state of the CertificateAuthority.

fields.label: Gcs Bucket
fields.help: The name of a Cloud Storage bucket where this CertificateAuthority will publish content, such as the CA certificate and CRLs.

fields.label: Ignore Active Certificates On Deletion
fields.help: This field allows the CA to be deleted even if the CA has active certs.

fields.label: Lifetime
fields.help: The desired lifetime of the CA certificate.

fields.label: Location
fields.help: Location of the CertificateAuthority.

fields.label: Pem Ca Certificate
fields.help: The signed CA certificate issued from the subordinated CA's CSR.

fields.label: Pool
fields.help: The name of the CaPool this Certificate Authority belongs to.

fields.label: Skip Grace Period
fields.help: If this flag is set, the Certificate Authority will be deleted as soon as possible without a 30-day grace period where undeletion would have been allowed.

fields.label: Type
fields.help: The Type of this CertificateAuthority.

fields.label: Config
Subject Config
Subject
Common Name
fields.help: The common name of the distinguished name.

fields.label: Country Code
fields.help: The country code of the subject.

fields.label: Locality
fields.help: The locality or city of the subject.

fields.label: Organization
fields.help: The organization of the subject.

fields.label: Organizational Unit
fields.help: The organizational unit of the subject.

fields.label: Postal Code
fields.help: The postal code of the subject.

fields.label: Province
fields.help: The province, territory, or regional state of the subject.

fields.label: Street Address
fields.help: The street address of the subject.
Contains distinguished name fields such as the location and organization.

fields.label: Subject Alt Name
DNS Names
fields.help: Contains only valid, fully-qualified host names.

fields.label: Email Addresses
fields.help: Contains only valid RFC 2822 E-mail addresses.

fields.label: IP Addresses
fields.help: Contains only valid 32-bit IPv4 addresses or RFC 4291 IPv6 addresses.

fields.label: Uris
fields.help: Contains only valid RFC 3986 URIs.
The subject alternative name fields.
Specifies some of the values in a certificate that are related to the subject.

fields.label: Subject Key ID
Key ID
fields.help: The value of the KeyId in lowercase hexadecimal.
When specified this provides a custom SKI to be used in the certificate.

fields.label: X509 Config
Aia Ocsp Servers
fields.help: Describes Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) endpoint addresses that appear in the "Authority Information Access" extension in the certificate.

fields.label: Additional Extensions
Critical
fields.help: Indicates whether or not this extension is critical (i.e., if the client does not know how to handle this extension, the client should consider this to be an error).

fields.label: Value
fields.help: The value of this X.509 extension.

fields.label: Object ID
fields.help: Describes values that are relevant in a CA certificate.
Specifies an X.509 extension, which may be used in different parts of X.509 objects like certificates, CSRs, and CRLs.

fields.label: Ca Options
Is Ca
fields.help: When true, the "CA" in Basic Constraints extension will be set to true.

fields.label: Max Issuer Path Length
fields.help: Refers to the "path length constraint" in Basic Constraints extension.

fields.label: Non Ca
fields.help: When true, the "CA" in Basic Constraints extension will be set to false.

fields.label: Zero Max Issuer Path Length
fields.help: When true, the "path length constraint" in Basic Constraints extension will be set to 0.
Describes values that are relevant in a CA certificate.

fields.label: Key Usage
Base Key Usage
Cert Sign
fields.help: The key may be used to sign certificates.

fields.label: Content Commitment
fields.help: The key may be used for cryptographic commitments.

fields.label: Crl Sign
fields.help: The key may be used sign certificate revocation lists.

fields.label: Data Encipherment
fields.help: The key may be used to encipher data.

fields.label: Decipher Only
fields.help: The key may be used to decipher only.

fields.label: Digital Signature
fields.help: The key may be used for digital signatures.

fields.label: Encipher Only
fields.help: The key may be used to encipher only.

fields.label: Key Agreement
fields.help: The key may be used in a key agreement protocol.

fields.label: Key Encipherment
fields.help: The key may be used to encipher other keys.
Describes high-level ways in which a key may be used.

fields.label: Extended Key Usage
Client Auth
fields.help: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2.

fields.label: Code Signing
fields.help: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3.

fields.label: Email Protection
fields.help: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.4.

fields.label: Ocsp Signing
fields.help: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.9.

fields.label: Server Auth
fields.help: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1.

fields.label: Time Stamping
fields.help: Corresponds to OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.8.
Describes high-level ways in which a key may be used.

fields.label: Unknown Extended Key Usages
fields.help: An ObjectId specifies an object identifier (OID).
Indicates the intended use for keys that correspond to a certificate.

fields.label: Name Constraints
Critical
fields.help: Indicates whether or not the name constraints are marked critical.

fields.label: Excluded DNS Names
fields.help: Contains excluded DNS names.

fields.label: Excluded Email Addresses
fields.help: Contains the excluded email addresses.

fields.label: Excluded IP Ranges
fields.help: Contains the excluded IP ranges.

fields.label: Excluded Uris
fields.help: Contains the excluded URIs that apply to the host part of the name.

fields.label: Permitted DNS Names
fields.help: Contains permitted DNS names.

fields.label: Permitted Email Addresses
fields.help: Contains the permitted email addresses.

fields.label: Permitted IP Ranges
fields.help: Contains the permitted IP ranges.

fields.label: Permitted Uris
fields.help: Contains the permitted URIs that apply to the host part of the name.
Describes the X.509 name constraints extension.

fields.label: Policy Ids
fields.help: Describes the X.509 certificate policy object identifiers, per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.4.
Describes how some of the technical X.509 fields in a certificate should be populated.
The config used to create a self-signed X.509 certificate or CSR.

fields.label: Key Spec
Algorithm
fields.help: The algorithm to use for creating a managed Cloud KMS key for a for a simplified experience.

fields.label: Cloud KMS Key Version
fields.help: The resource name for an existing Cloud KMS CryptoKeyVersion in the format 'projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*/cryptoKeyVersions/*'.
Used when issuing certificates for this CertificateAuthority.

fields.label: Subordinate Config
Certificate Authority
fields.help: This can refer to a CertificateAuthority that was used to create a subordinate CertificateAuthority.

fields.label: Pem Issuer Chain
Pem Certificates
fields.help: Expected to be in leaf-to-root order according to RFC 5246.
Contains the PEM certificate chain for the issuers of this CertificateAuthority, but not pem certificate for this CA itself.
If this is a subordinate CertificateAuthority, this field will be set with the subordinate configuration, which describes its issuers.

fields.label: User Defined Access Urls
Aia Issuing Certificate Urls
fields.help: A list of URLs where this CertificateAuthority's CA certificate is published that is specified by users.

fields.label: Crl Access Urls
fields.help: A list of URLs where this CertificateAuthority's CRLs are published that is specified by users.
Custom URLs for accessing content published by this CA, such as the CA certificate and CRLs, that can be specified by users.
